title: Glaucoma, cataracts and the possibility of a cornea transplant
summary: Poor health, hospital stays and glaucoma and cataracts made him leave the band, and doctors have discussed a cornea transplant.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Why did you leave, Herman? I gather the band kept on going, you say with someone else in your place.
Yes, well I've been sickly, so I was in and out of this hospital and that hospital for one thing, and my eyes --
Well, I have glaucoma, and cataracts, and all that junk. And the left eye, the -- they're talking -- they're still talking about doing a -- a cornea transplant.

And they -- I've got to go back to them. I've got to return the thing there, and the doctor say he going to wait a while and take another look. I was in there two weeks ago. And I've been doing that for the last
Well did it -- did your eyes go all of a sudden, or had they been bothering you for a while?
No, they were bothering me for a while, yes. They were bothering me for a while, and --
Had you used glasses at all?

Oh yeah, I wore glasses for years, and I had -- had contacts, but decided that when I was working the pit bands, theaters, playing shows, I was wearing glasses (unintelligible). In fact, I was blind once upon a time, just for how many weeks? Ah, two or three months, I guess.
